positions.commentary: The speaker identifies Micron Technology as his largest current position, explaining his thesis that the memory business changed from a terrible business with too many players to one with three rational players.

The speaker states that for the artificial intelligence and blockchain game, no matter where the future goes, you need an Nvidia graphics card to run it, and he likes the upside scenario for the industry with rapid change.
The speaker mentions Amazon as an example of a business they missed because they were too dense to figure it out 18-20 years ago, but notes they don't pay a penalty for passing on a great business.
The speaker discusses his past Fiat Chrysler investment which included Ferrari, noting he sold the stock before understanding the business and realizing its unique position.
The speaker marvels at Starbucks as an incredible business with fast payback periods and strong demand driven by convenience, but admits they always thought it was expensive and never bought it.

thesis: This episode argues that the memory and semiconductor industries have undergone a fundamental shift from a fragmented market to one dominated by a few rational players, creating significant opportunities for investors. It highlights specific positions like Micron Technology and Nvidia as beneficiaries of this change and the broader artificial intelligence and blockchain ecosystem. The speaker also reflects on past missed opportunities and the unique nature of his investment approach as a single-player game.
